cohort: The study included pregnant women with previous bariatric surgery (n=52) compared to two control groups: one matched for pre-surgery BMI (n=104) and another matched for pre-pregnancy BMI (n=104), all from a French administrative county.
finding: Bariatric surgery reduced the risks of excessive fetal growth and gestational diabetes, with a trend for a higher risk of small-for-gestational-age infants, even when matched on pre-pregnancy BMI.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight of 2960 +- 545g in the BS group, compared to 3381 +- 735g in group A and 3310 +- 645g in group B.
